svg.title: Event Sourcing
svg.desc: Event Sourcing. Store every change as an immutable event and rebuild state by replaying them. Step 1, Append, don't overwrite: Withdraw 30: the handler checks balance 70, then appends event #4. Nothing is updated or deleted. Step 2, Replay to rebuild state: Replay #1 to #4 and the balance goes 0, 100, 70, 40. A snapshot at version 4 shortens later loads. Step 3, Project and subscribe: The same events feed read models and other subscribers; a view added later replays from #1. Step 4, Correct by appending: A mistaken deposit is reversed by appending #6, not edited. History still answers: 70 as of #3.

g.text: Withdraw 30: the handler checks balance 70, then appends event #4. Nothing is updated or deleted.
Replay #1 to #4 and the balance goes 0, 100, 70, 40. A snapshot at version 4 shortens later loads.
The same events feed read models and other subscribers; a view added later replays from #1.
A mistaken deposit is reversed by appending #6, not edited. History still answers: 70 as of #3.
Append only: nothing is updated or deleted.
Another writer appended first? Rejected: reload the stream and retry.
Current state is a fold over the events:
The log is the source of truth; views are disposable.
Subscribers lag slightly behind the stream: eventual consistency.
History is never edited: a compensating event corrects it.
Both stay in the audit trail, and any past state can be replayed.
UPDATE accounts SET balance = 40 WHERE id = 42
One row holds only the latest value.
What happened, and why, is lost.
no history: the row is the only record
every event, every time: slower as the stream grows
… then only the events after version 4
A snapshot is only a cache of the fold: delete it and the replay still gives 40.
Deposit 500 went to the wrong account
no UPDATE or DELETE of event #5
